stories.headline: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize as US imposes sanctions on International Criminal Court
stories.body:
South African judge Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize [c1].

The Trump administration announced sanctions targeting the International Criminal Court as an institution [c2]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the sanctions ban US entities from financial transactions with the court [c3]. Rubio warned that either the court ends its threats or the US will end the court [c4]. The court was founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide [c5]. It currently has 125 member states [c5]. But the United States, Russia, China, India, and Israel are not member states [c9].

The United States gave a six-month grace period before certain sanctions take effect [c6]. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US decision a serious blow to collective criminal justice [c7]. He said the court is a key pillar of that justice [c7]. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions [c8]. Netanyahu called the court a political body that threatens democratic sovereignty [c8].

vocab.meaning: a country's power to govern itself
penalties imposed on a country or group

stories.headline: US agrees deal with Russia to import diesel despite opposition from Ukraine and lawmakers
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Moscow to supply diesel to global markets [c10]. The deal permits Russia to sell diesel to the United States and other countries [c10].

The US Treasury Department issued a temporary licence to support the agreement [c11]. The licence suspends sanctions on Russian diesel exports through April 7, 2027 [c11]. Russia will supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately [c12]. It will supply 500,000 tonnes in November [c12]. Moscow will then export 1 million tonnes shortly after [c12]. It is scheduled to export another 3 million tonnes depending on refinery conditions [c12].

President Donald Trump reached the diesel agreement during a phone call with Vladimir Putin [c17]. The two leaders originally scheduled the call to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia [c17].

Fuel prices in the United States were high before the deal [c14, c18]. The average price of diesel in the US stood at $6.28 per gallon at the time of the announcement [c14]. That price was down from a record $6.53 per gallon in late September [c14]. Average regular gasoline prices in the US rose more than 46 percent since late February to reach $4.37 per gallon [c18]. US diesel prices increased 67 percent over the same time frame [c18].

Russia faced production problems before the agreement [c15]. Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries caused Russia's diesel production to fall by an estimated 30 percent [c15].

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the new agreement [c13]. Zelenskyy said that easing sanctions on Russian energy plays into Moscow's hands [c13]. He said the move prolongs the war [c13].

American politicians also criticized the move [c16]. Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen condemned President Donald Trump for lifting sanctions on Russian fossil fuels [c16]. Several Republican lawmakers also condemned Trump for lifting the sanctions [c16].

vocab.meaning: an official document giving permission to do something
factories that process raw materials like oil

stories.headline: Strong earthquake hits Panama causing infrastructure damage and economic losses
stories.body:
A 7.6-magnitude earthquake struck Panama near the community of Pitaloza Arriba [c19]. The US Geological Survey also registered the main earthquake at magnitude 7.7 at a depth of 12.6 kilometers [c24]. It was the strongest quake in that part of Panama since at least 1951 [c24].

Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino appealed for calm after the earthquake [c20]. Mulino wrote on X that what happened should not generate alarm and disorder [c20]. Preliminary estimates from the US Geological Survey show economic losses in Panama will likely exceed $1 billion [c25].

The quake caused structural collapses and damage in Penonomé [c21]. Damaged sites include the St John Baptist Cathedral, the governor's office building, and the Dos Continentes hotel [c21]. Panama's Ministry of Education ordered schools across the country to close [c27].

Transportation was disrupted in several areas [c22, c26]. Tocumen International Airport in Panama City temporarily suspended flights and evacuated facilities for safety checks [c22]. Panama City's Metro system halted service on lines 1 and 2 as a precaution [c26]. But the Panama Canal Authority confirmed ship traffic continued normally [c23].

Earlier in 2026, twin earthquakes in Venezuela killed at least 6,500 people in June [c28]. A magnitude 7.4 quake in Colombia killed at least 289 people in August [c28].

vocab.meaning: an action taken to prevent possible harm
coming before the main or final result

stories.headline: Delhi authorities deploy heavy security and restrict transit ahead of opposition protest
stories.body:
The Cockroach Janta Party called on supporters to gather at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, 2026 [c31]. The group released a poster demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar [c31]. They also demanded the rollback of the Special Intensive Revision [c31].

Delhi Police denied permission for the planned protest at Jantar Mantar [c32]. Officers cited alleged rule violations during an earlier demonstration by the group [c32]. Delhi Police sent a letter on October 9 to CJP co-convener Saurav Das and joint secretary Balkrishna [c40]. Police said their communication on October 7 was not a proper application submitted 10 days in advance [c40]. Police also said Jantar Mantar has an official capacity to hold about 1,000 people at a time [c42].

Authorities took major security measures across the city [c33]. Officials deployed 23,000 security personnel and closed 45 metro stations across Delhi [c33]. The Union Ministry of Home Affairs directed all States and Union Territories to coordinate with Delhi Police [c34]. They were instructed to stop protesters from moving toward Delhi [c34].

Security forces also made local detentions [c36]. NSUI Jamia Millia Islamia Secretary Ebin Basil reported that police detained four female students near Jamia around 11:30 p.m. [c36]. He said police released them around 3 a.m. [c36].

The Centre alleged that over 200 police personnel were injured during a CJP protest in July [c37]. Delhi Police said they identified 2,873 people using CCTV footage from a July 20 march [c41]. Police claimed 989 of those identified had criminal antecedents [c41].

Despite the actions, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged supporters to continue [c35]. Dipke said on X that he would reach Delhi by 9:30 a.m. [c35]. He urged protesters to keep going even if he is detained [c35].

Union Minister Chirag Paswan said the protesters are the youth of India and nobody can stop them [c29]. Paswan had previously called for clarification about Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's decision-making [c30]. But Paswan backed out after the Election Commission said decisions were unanimous [c30].

In an open letter, 42 retired judges defended Gyanesh Kumar [c38]. They criticized the CJP-led protests against the Election Commission of India [c38]. Political protests against the commission have occurred before [c39]. In May 2014, the BJP staged protests against the Election Commission after candidate Narendra Modi was denied permission to hold a rally in Varanasi [c39].

vocab.meaning: a person's past history or background

stories.headline: US suspends PERM green card processing for major technology companies
stories.body:
The Trump administration suspended eight major tech companies from the US PERM program on October 8 [c43]. The affected firms include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, and Capgemini [c43]. US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced that authorities will stop accepting new applications and processing pending ones for these companies [c44].

US Vice President JD Vance urged US companies to hire great American workers instead of foreign indentured servants [c51]. India's Ministry of External Affairs called Vance's comments deeply offensive and unwarranted [c52]. The ministry issued an official statement on October 9 regarding the immigration restrictions [c47].

Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said talent mobility adds value to both the Indian and US economies [c53]. He said Indian talent helps US companies with cutting-edge work and job creation [c53]. The ministry noted that existing H-1B visas remain valid, though Indian nationals received 71 percent of all H-1B visas in the 2023-24 financial year [c45, c50].

Tata Consultancy Services said in a stock filing that it submitted fewer than 10 PERM applications over two years [c46]. It still plans to hire 15,000 US workers over five years [c46]. Pan IIT Alumni India Chairman Prabhat Kumar urged graduates to return to India, saying a visa was never a stable foundation [c48, c49].

stories.headline: Assembly and parliamentary bypoll election results declared across Indian states
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said recent bypoll election victories reflect public connection with the ruling coalition's agenda [c67].

In Tamil Nadu, political party TVK won two assembly seats in Dharapuram and Madurantakam [c54]. Candidate P Sathyabama won Dharapuram by 9,471 votes, while Maragatham Kumaravel won Madurantakam by 20,040 votes [c55]. The wins increased TVK's total in the 234-member assembly from 107 to 109 seats [c56].

In West Bengal, the BJP retained the Nandigram seat and won Rejinagar from AJUP [c57]. BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar won Rejinagar with 1,29,914 votes, beating Golam Nabi Azad [c65]. In Nandigram, BJP's Hasirani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan by 1,22,753 votes [c66].

In Assam, BJP candidate Devasish Sharma won the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat by over 1.5 lakh votes against AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal [c59]. Following the loss, Raijor Dal chief Akhil Gogoi demanded the resignation of Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi [c62]. Gogoi said that Congress's minority vote share in Nagaon dropped from 25 percent to 5 percent [c63]. In Puducherry, AINRC candidate Ashok Anand won the Thattanchavady seat by over 8,400 votes [c60].

vocab.meaning: a special election held to fill a vacant seat
a temporary alliance of political parties
